title: Recipe Manager
prompt:
Implement a `RecipeManager` that stores recipes with an ID, a name, and a list of ingredients. Recipe IDs are strings.

Required methods:
- `add_recipe(recipe_id, name, ingredients)` returns `True` and stores the recipe unless the ID already exists or another recipe has the same case-insensitive name. Otherwise return `False`.
- `get_recipe(recipe_id)` returns `{'id': ..., 'name': ..., 'ingredients': ...}` or `None`.
- `update_recipe(recipe_id, name, ingredients)` returns `True` only when the recipe exists and the proposed case-insensitive name is not used by a different recipe. Changing only the capitalization of its own name is allowed.
- `delete_recipe(recipe_id)` removes an existing recipe and returns `True`, otherwise returns `False`.
- `search_recipes(query)` returns recipes whose names contain `query`, case-insensitively. `get_all_recipes()` returns every recipe. Both lists are ordered by ingredient count ascending, then numeric recipe ID ascending.
- `add_user(user_id, username)` creates a user only if the user ID is new. `edit_recipe(user_id, recipe_id, name, ingredients)` applies the same update rules but returns `False` when the user does not exist.

Return recipe dictionaries in the same shape as `get_recipe`. You may assume recipe IDs used by sorting are decimal integer strings.

example.reasoning: A recipe is addressable by ID while name uniqueness is case-insensitive.
